title: Sleep-dependent microglial functions in Alzheimer’s disease
title_zh: 睡眠对阿尔茨海默病中小胶质细胞功能的影响
abstract: Sleep is a fundamental regulator of brain homeostasis, yet how distinct brain cell types contribute to this process remains poorly understood. Microglia, the resident immune cells of the central nervous system, actively regulate neuroinflammatory tone, metabolic waste clearance, and synaptic remodeling, thereby contributing to neural circuit maintenance and proteostasis. Delineating the different functions played by microglia during specific brain states, such as sleep, represents an active area of research. In this article, we review a growing literature supporting the notion that sleep dynamically shapes microglial functional outputs. We further suggest that the failure of the sleep-microglia axis may represent an important component of the molecular framework of Alzheimer's disease (AD), contributing to disease progression. Finally, we discuss preclinical and clinical evidence suggesting that sleep-targeting interventions may modulate AD pathology, and highlight the possibility that restoring sleep physiology could recalibrate microglial homeostatic functions and slow disease progression.
abstract_zh: 睡眠是大脑稳态的基本调节因子，但不同脑细胞类型如何参与这一过程仍不清楚。小胶质细胞是中枢神经系统的驻留免疫细胞，积极调节神经炎症水平、代谢废物清除和突触重塑，从而有助于神经回路维护和蛋白稳态。阐明小胶质细胞在特定脑状态（如睡眠）下的不同功能是当前的研究热点。本文综述了越来越多的文献，支持睡眠动态塑造小胶质细胞功能输出的观点。我们进一步提出，睡眠-小胶质细胞轴的失调可能是阿尔茨海默病（AD）分子框架的重要组成部分，促进疾病进展。最后，我们讨论了前临床和临床证据，表明针对睡眠的干预可能调节AD病理，并强调恢复睡眠生理可能重新校准小胶质细胞的稳态功能，减缓疾病进展。
